Concise Clinical Note

Consult Summary:
31-year-old male with 4-day history of intensely pruritic, sore, red dermatitis on chest, hands, and antecubital fossae; likely eczema flare.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Diffuse red, itchy, sore rash × 4 days, worst on chest, hands, inner elbows; interferes with sleep and work.  
• Associated symptoms: No fever, bleeding, pus, cough, dyspnea, bowel or urinary issues. Skin “cracked” in places.  
• Pertinent negatives: No facial involvement; no systemic symptoms.  
• Past medical history: Atopic eczema (previous flares responsive to topical therapy); remote asthma (inactive).  
• Medications tried: OTC topical steroid cream (name/dose/route/frequency not documented); OTC antihistamines (names/doses not documented) with little benefit. No regular prescriptions.  
• Allergies: Denies drug or other allergies.  
• Social: Lives with flatmates; full-time project manager in pharmaceutical company; non-smoker; drinks a few beers/week; enjoys hiking (limited by current symptoms). Preventive care not discussed.

Examination:
• Vitals: not documented.  
• Skin (telehealth visual + patient report): Diffuse erythematous, dry, cracked plaques on chest, hands, antecubital areas; appears eczematous; no visible exudate or bleeding.

Impression:
Eczema flare (atopic dermatitis exacerbation).

Plan:
• Prescribe stronger topical corticosteroid (specific agent/strength not documented).  
• Prescribe emollient for bath/shower use; apply regularly for 7–10 days.  
• Prescribe oral Fexofenadine (dose/frequency not documented) for pruritus; consider alternative antihistamines if inadequate.  
• Advise keeping diary of potential triggers (soaps, detergents, clothing, allergens).  
• Follow-up in 1 week if no improvement or sooner if worsening.

Quality checks:

● Missing expected elements: objective vitals; detailed skin exam description; full medication reconciliation (name/strength/frequency of prior steroid cream and antihistamines); vaccination status; family history.  
● Internal conflicts: Patient localizes rash to chest, hands, inner elbows; doctor later mentions chest and back (conflict noted).  
● Transcript quality: Moderate audio issues; some sentences partially inaudible but core clinical content understandable.
